subject: LumOS: request for expedited fallback and approval to mitigate p95 regression
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire@lumos.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement - LumOS <procurement@lumos.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance spike on LumOS pilot after model update

Hi Grace,

We're seeing a sudden p95 latency increase on the /v1/generate endpoint for our pilot tenants since your team rolled model 'redwood-model-3c' into our default route this morning. Baseline p95 was ~180ms; since ~09:30 PT it's trending ~520ms and some tails up to 900ms. Error rates are low, but user-facing latency is unacceptable for our SLA in the pilot.

Attached is a snapshot from our client-side telemetry (perf_snapshot_20261008.csv). Can your team advise whether there's an immediate fallback available? If we need to revert to the prior model variant for a short window, we need to know ETA and whether there are any billing/contract implications.

We're planning a sync with our SRE at 14:30 PT — if you can confirm mitigation options before then that would be great.

Thanks,
Claire
Lead SRE, LumOS

[attachment: perf_snapshot_20261008.csv (csv, 34KB)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@lumos.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance spike on LumOS pilot after model update

Claire — thanks for the heads up and for the snapshot. We're seeing the same p95 drift in our edge telemetry correlated with the new attention kernel shipped in model-3c at 09:10 PT.

Immediate proposal (need quick internal sign-off):
- Enable expedited variant fallback: route LumOS production traffic back to model-2.1-quant (exact match of prior variant).
- Apply a temporary traffic split for the pilot (100% -> model-2.1-quant) while we triage.
- Reduce batching window for their route to 8ms to avoid aggregation-induced latency spikes.

Risks/costs: temporary increase in qps/instances if we disable batching; estimated incremental cost ~+12% for the next 6 hours. If legal/procurement needs a notification, Marissa can own comms.

Marcus / Lauren / Rishi — can we get a green light to implement the fallback and the batching change now? If so, I'll notify LumOS and proceed with the canary rollback per the playbook.

—Grace
Director, Customer Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Nguyen <claire@lumos.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2026 13:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance spike on LumOS pilot after model update

Agree with Grace's mitigation. Operationally:
1) I can flip the route to model-2.1-quant for LumOS immediately and run a 10-minute canary at 10% traffic. If canary looks good, we'll move to 100% within 15 minutes.
2) We'll also change the batching window as Grace requested; I'll coordinate with infra to ensure no cold-start burst.
3) Post-fallback we'll capture 60 minutes of high-res traces and KV cache snapshots for regression analysis.

Approvals needed from:
- Product (for rolling back a verified model change) — Lauren will weigh in on risk/compatibility.
- Finance (cost bump awareness) — Marissa can notify Procurement if LumOS requires billing notes.

I'll prepare the canary_playbook_v2.md and share it in-channel; implementing on my mark.

—Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Nguyen <claire@lumos.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance spike on LumOS pilot after model update

On Fri, Oct 8, 2026 at 1:35 PM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'll prepare the canary_playbook_v2.md and share it in-channel; implementing on my mark.

Two points from the ops/play perspective:
- Rollback plan: do a phased rollback -> 10% canary (10m) -> 50% (10m) -> 100% (monitor 30m). If we see tail regressions after 50% we stop and revert traffic.
- Observability gates: p95, p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and request queuing time. If p95 > 250ms or gpu_util jumps >20% we pause the rollout.

Cost/contract note: short rollback (<= 6 hours) is covered under our support terms; procurement notification only if LumOS requests account credits.

I'll be available to execute the rollback; Marcus can run the routing change. Lauren — please confirm product acceptability for the temporary variant.

—Rishi
Head of Product Operations

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Performance spike on LumOS pilot after model update

Team — proceeding with the mitigation now per approvals:
- Marcus: please start the 10% canary to model-2.1-quant at 09:50 ET.
- Rishi: I'll monitor the p95/p99 dashboards and traces; stop the rollout on your gate thresholds.
- Marissa: please flag Procurement only if LumOS requests any retro credits; otherwise send a short notice email that an emergency rollback was performed.

Claire — we expect the canary + ramp to complete within ~30 minutes; I will update this thread as soon as the rollback reaches 100% and stability is observed. Thanks for raising this quickly.

—Grace
Director, Customer Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
